sections.eyebrow: What a project can look like

items.title: Business websites
items.description: A structured website that explains your business, presents your services and makes contact details easy to find.

sections.heading: From a first conversation to a considered handoff.
sections.description: Clear review points keep the work grounded in the agreed brief.

items.name: Understand the brief
items.desc: Discuss the audience, objectives and constraints, then define deliverables and responsibilities.

items.name: Agree the plan
items.desc: Confirm the scope, review stages and timeline before production begins.

items.name: Develop a direction
items.desc: Create the agreed structure, designs or campaign materials for review.

items.name: Refine the work
items.desc: Consolidate feedback around the brief and resolve agreed changes.

items.name: Prepare the final work
items.desc: Complete the agreed checks and package the deliverables or launch requirements.

items.name: Discuss next steps
items.desc: Confirm ownership, documentation and any separately scoped ongoing support.

sections.heading: Bring the context. We will help shape the brief.
sections.description: You do not need a finished specification. A few useful starting points make the first conversation more productive.
items: Your website URL, if you have one
The pages and user actions that matter most
Available copy, brand assets and images
Your target launch date and practical constraints

items.question: Can you improve an existing website?
items.answer: Yes, a review can identify where structure, content or usability could improve. The team will confirm what can be retained and what needs rebuilding.

items.question: Are hosting and maintenance included?
items.answer: Hosting, domains and ongoing support depend on the agreed scope. Ask which costs and responsibilities are included before the project begins.

items.question: What content should I provide?
items.answer: Prepare your services, contact details, brand assets and any existing copy or images. The discovery conversation will identify gaps and content responsibilities.

items.question: How do you estimate timing and fees?
items.answer: The team will review your brief, available materials and deliverables before sharing a project-specific estimate. Changes in scope can affect both timing and cost.
